dialogue.name: Father Anselm
dialogue.prompt: Press E to talk to Father Anselm

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: You came up from Caernarfon, Father. Twelve years, is it. You could go back.

band.name: Father Anselm
band.line: A younger son with good Latin and no living, Sir Roger. The justiciar's chapel has a dozen of those. This one has a roll nobody else can read and a stair nobody else sleeps over.

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: They say the old King's heart is under your altar stone, Father, in a lead box sent up from Vantry the year he died, so that some part of him should see the place finished.

band.name: Father Anselm
band.line: I have had a bar under that stone once, Sir Roger, and I will not tell you what I found, because whichever way it went it is a scandal, and I have enough of those.

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: They say Sir Walter's own coffer covered what the works had lost, before he died, and that is the whole reason his books balanced.

band.name: Father Anselm
band.line: I have read his accounts, Sir Roger. I have also heard what you just said from three other mouths, each swearing he had it from a fourth.

band.name: Father Anselm
band.line: I keep a knuckle of bone under glass on the north sill, Sir Roger, and call it Saint Osyth's own.

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: And do you believe that, Father, or only say it?

band.name: Father Anselm
band.line: On my better days, both.

band.name: Master Robert
band.line: The lodge has it that a hod-carrier went off the Bakehouse Tower's scaffold in the ninth year and stood up laughing, for calling on Cadeyrn on the way down.

band.name: Thomas Wykes
band.line: They also say it was a load of straw broke his fall and not the saint. I have hauled that straw. It was a great deal of straw.

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: Give the outer ward its head and it would drink the cellar dry and leave the walk door standing open besides.

band.name: Piers Marrable
band.line: A firm hand is the whole of what keeps this castle a castle and not a March village with better stone around it, Sir Roger. I have always said so.

band.name: Piers Marrable
band.line: The Sunder War is two years settled, Sir Roger. When does the coin catch up with the peace?

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: When Caernarfon says it does. I have stopped asking twice a year and started asking once.

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: Eleven years married, Piers, and eight of them here. I had twelve men at Bryn Adda and thought myself a Constable. I have eight now and a wall, and think myself less of one.

band.name: Piers Marrable
band.line: And a wife whose brother sits among the justiciar's clerks, Sir Roger, which you have never once mentioned and never once forgotten.

band.name: Piers Marrable
band.line: There is an alderman's family in Mereford that has not paid its wall-tax in a decade, if the roll were ever made to say so.

band.name: Sir Roger
band.line: And whose hand keeps the roll from saying so, Piers? I ask it in this hall, and I would not have it asked past the door.

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: [Dafydd is got up onto the bench end, and the benches take up the time with their cups]

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: Forty Michaelmas, and the roof not on, and the King that began it dead and gone;

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: six for the curtain and ten for the towers, and the rest of it built in the King's spare hours!

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: Eight men watching where eighty stood, and three months' wages made good in wood!

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: [the high table laughs half a beat late; the Constable's cup goes down an inch and comes back up]

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: There is a verse about a writ, and a verse about a river. Those two I do not sing in the King's tongue.

band.name: Dafydd ap Rhys
band.line: [he sings them anyway, and the benches have every word of them, and the high table has none]

band.name: Dafydd
band.line: My grandfather stood on the other bank of this river against the old King for nine years, Master Robert, and was sworn at the end of it, and kept his word and his opinions both. I stand the King's watch and I have the opinions.

band.name: Master Robert
band.line: And the song, I suppose. I have sat at the high table and heard the garrison sing it every Michaelmas I have kept the works, and never been told a word of what it says.

band.name: Dafydd
band.line: Not one man of the watch will draw from the south-west well after dark. Not one, and every one of them a different reason why.

band.name: Marged
band.line: The water tastes the same to me at any hour, and I am the one who has actually tried it after dark.

band.name: Nest
band.line: The inner ward eats first, warms first and is paid first, Master Robert, whatever the works go without.

band.name: Master Robert
band.line: The inner ward would say the same of you and mean the opposite. That is the whole of what a wall is for.

band.name: Marged
band.line: Michaelmas day the town has this whole ward by charter, Prime to Vespers, stalls from the lodge to the hall, and the garrison stands on the walk and watches its own yard fill up with the people it keeps out the rest of the year.

band.name: Nest
band.line: And for one day the only tongue in the outer ward is our own, and the inner ward stands at its gate and does not understand a word, and that is the best of it.

band.name: Marged
band.line: That cousin of yours reads a frost off a cat's back better than any almanac I ever paid for.

band.name: Nest
band.line: She is no cousin of mine past what the roll says, and I never said the charm was worth the penny. I never said it wasn't, either.

band.name: Marged
band.line: Nest says the well tastes of rock and she draws from it every day of her life. That is the whole of what I know about the well.

band.name: Dafydd
band.line: They say it goes down to the river and the tide comes up in it, and a man with a boat and a sack could poison the castle from the quay. Nobody who says it has lowered a light.

band.name: Dafydd
band.line: My grandfather swore the chapel bell was a shrine bell off the March once, melted down so no native hand would ring it.

band.name: Marged
band.line: Your grandfather swore a great many things, Dafydd ap Rhys, and I never saw him show me the shrine.

band.name: Dafydd
band.line: There is a cross cut in the stone for every man who died building this place. Count them and you have the priest's roll without the Latin.

band.name: Master Robert
band.line: A cross goes at the springing of an arch, Dafydd, and it means the arch. The watch has counted them twice and got two numbers, and neither of them was the roll.

band.name: Marged
band.line: Madoc tells whoever stands at his bars that something moves under the Prison Tower's floor at night. Slow. A drag, then a stop, same as it has since before they put him in to hear it.

band.name: Nest
band.line: He has said that every day this week, Marged, and I have believed him every day this week, and neither of those has got him out.
